Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me specifically what antibiotic you were prescribed and when you started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Patient
text: izations are up to date. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Acute appendicitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) Syndrome secondary to suspected antibiotic use. The mention of "Acute appendicitis" by the previous doctor appears to be a misdiagnosis based on the classic triad of fever, rash, and joint pain following antibiotic initiation. We have ordered blood work and skin images to confirm eosinophilia, atypical lymphocytes, and the rash pattern characteristic of DRESS.
